Majority at 218 seats out of 435. Generic Ballot (likely voters): D +7.35. Probabilities conditional on a Democrat-versus-Republican contest in each district. Updated October 1, 2026.

The engine produces the 435 predictive distributions and the national balance of power. It is recomputed every day with the latest polls. The probabilities assume a Democrat-versus-Republican contest in each district: uncontested seats, same-party contests and third parties are not modeled. This is a provisional forecast, not a scientific certification.

THE MILLÉNAIRE METHOD

An explicit baseline. Documented tests.

RECHECK · 21 SEPT. 2026
01

Start from the results

The electoral baseline separates the presidential reference from local persistence. The project folder's parameters remain unchanged.

02

Separate the information

The national signal, district polls and local effects remain separately identified. Unverified data are not included.

03

Measuring past error

The gaps shown here are recomputed on the archives of 2010, 2014 and 2018. A historical performance is not a guarantee for 2026.

1,016 cycle-district pairs observed at three horizons, i.e. 3,048 rows, but only three distinct elections. The control 2022 to J−50 is not the complete integrated backtest. [5]

Parameters and status of the layers +

Retained parameters

Local persistence: incumbent α = 0.57; open seat α = 0.18. National sensitivity: β = 1. These coefficients remain unchanged; only the uncertainty components were estimated for the engine.

District polls

Specification M3 pre-registered, τ = 4 points, meets its historical criterion 2018. Replication on a second cycle remains open; its overall status remains A_MESURER.

Uncertainty

Historical residuals were used to estimate national, regional, state and district variances by nested moments, after correcting for noise in group means. The national component was recalibrated on October 1, 2026, of 0.980 to 1.457 point: this is the engine's measured national error at T−60. The region components (0.478), State (1.430) and district (3.937) are unchanged. Overall validation remains limited to three cycles. Unit: points of two-party D share.

Layers not included

Finance, conditional special elections and fundamentals: NON_MESURE. Second additive incumbency correction and group elasticities: REJECTED in the source registry.

One engine run.
A provisional forecast.

200,000 correlated draws are recomputed every day. This page shows the outputs of engine M2, with the canonical prior unchanged, published as a provisional forecast. M3 remains excluded; electoral cases outside the D/R contest, geography and full national calibration are not certified by this run.

Sources and reference dates

[1] Institution. U.S. House of Representatives. 435 voting representatives; 218 is the absolute majority of 435.

[2] Engine outputs: forecast_us_2026.json, calculation of October 1, 2026 (HOUSE-GB-REFRESH-20261001). Generic Ballot under rule Common V3, polls through October 1, 2026.

[3] Local reference. Corrected canonical prior V3. The page uses the historical field pres24, not the prior's score 2026. Values rounded to two decimals on screen.

[4] District polls. Local aggregate V1, project snapshot v8. No score from an unverified primary source is shown.

[5] Validation. Historical validation handoff, recheck of September 21, 2026. The metrics M0/M1/M2 come from archived values, without re-estimation.

About this edition. House V7: carried over from V6, shared banner of the Berlin reference, cartogram and geographic views. Model and prior unchanged. Viewing some Drive files requires authorization.

[6] Geography. Census TIGERweb, 120th Congress; Missouri: 119th Congress. Census warning on Missouri. Identifier check 435/435 before display; any latest court-ordered change is not certified by this load alone.
